title: [C15T2] - Tourists visiting a particular Caribbean island
prompt: The graph below shows the number of tourists (measured in millions) visiting a particular Caribbean island between 2010 and 2017. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates how many tourists travelled to a particular Caribbean island between 2010 and 2017, showing figures for visitors accommodated on cruise ships, those staying on the island, and the total number of visitors.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, all three categories showed an upward trend during the given period, despite some fluctuations. Additionally, cruise ship visitors experienced the most significant growth, and while island-based tourists initially outnumbered cruise ship passengers, this pattern reversed by 2016.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the two accommodation types, in 2010, 0.75 million tourists stayed on the island, which was three times higher than the 0.25 million who chose cruise ships. Cruise ship travelers subsequently demonstrated the most volatile yet dramatic growth, initially rising to 0.5 million in 2011 before dipping back to 0.25 million in 2012, then surging consistently from 0.5 million in 2013 to 2 million by 2017. In contrast, island-based visitors showed a more moderate pattern, increasing steadily to peak at 1.5 million in 2013, maintaining this level through 2015, before declining to 1.25 million in 2016 and recovering to 1.5 million in the final year.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the total number of visitors, the figure started at 1 million in 2010. The total then demonstrated steady growth throughout most of the period, reaching 2.75 million in 2015, remaining unchanged in 2016, before experiencing a significant jump to 3.5 million visitors in 2017.
